sources.entry: rem - An open source approach to locally record and enable searching everything you view on your Mac. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jasonjmcghee/rem) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: rem is an experimental open-source macOS app that records your screen every 2 seconds locally and makes everything you've viewed searchable and browsable.
summary.what_it_does: rem takes a screenshot every 2 seconds, runs text recognition on each capture, and stores the results in a local SQLite database alongside video recordings. It provides a full-screen timeline scrubber for moving back through what you have viewed, and lets you copy text from past screens. Keyword search covers the recorded history and can be filtered by application, with clicking a result jumping to that point in the timeline. A "Copy Recent Context" action builds an LLM prompt from recently seen content. The README says it works with external monitors and includes an Intel build alongside Apple Silicon.
use_cases: search text on screen from earlier in the day
review what you looked at on your Mac
copy text from a past screen
give an LLM recent on-screen context
keep a private local record of screen activity
how_to_run: Download the latest release, or build it yourself
Launch the app and click the brain icon, then click "Start Remembering"
Click "Open timeline" or press Cmd + Scroll Up to open the timeline view
notable: Fully local recording with no telemetry or tracking, per the README
Full-screen timeline scrubber for going back in time
Live Text integration for selecting text in the timeline
Copy Recent Context action to build LLM prompts from recent screens
Storage location is documented in the FAQ and can be opened from the menu bar
caveats: README calls it very alpha; only tested on Apple Silicon, with Intel build newly added and needing testing
Natural language and vector search, more filters, fine-grained purging, and first-class multi-monitor support are unchecked roadmap items
Build from source requires cloning with submodules and building through Xcode
